title: Water Cycle Basics
summary: This lesson explores the water cycle and how water moves above and below the Earth's surface. Students will examine the four main stages: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.

sections.text: Scene: A diagram displays the Earth's surface with blue arrows pointing above and below to show movement. The layout is split into upper sky regions and lower ground and water areas. I wonder...? What does the water cycle describe? Answer: The water cycle describes how water moves above and below the Earth surface.

Scene: Bright yellow sun rays point down toward liquid water, showing heat turning the liquid into vapor. Higher up in the sky, the vapor cools to form visible white clouds. I wonder...? How do clouds form? Answer: Condensation forms clouds when vapor cools high in the sky.

Scene: Rain and snow fall down from the clouds toward the ground, while runoff flows into rivers, lakes, and oceans. Blue arrows trace the water returning and gathering together. I wonder...? What gathers runoff into rivers, lakes and oceans? Answer: Collection gathers runoff into rivers, lakes and oceans.

key_concepts: Water movement above and below the Earth surface
Evaporation using heat from the sun
Condensation forming clouds when vapor cools
Precipitation returning water as rain or snow
Collection gathering runoff into rivers, lakes and oceans
learning_objectives: Describe how water moves above and below the Earth surface
Identify the roles of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection
Explain how heat from the sun and cooling vapor drive the cycle
